analysis.title: Tracking U.S. Supply Chain Congestion: GS Supply Chain Congestion Scale, Nov 23rd; Index Lower W/W, Bottleneck Scale Unchanged at '2'
key_insights: Weekly bottleneck scale was unchanged at 2 for the week of 11/23/2026, while the congestion index fell 11% w/w. Levels remain well below peak congestion (scale 10) and are in line with pre-Covid fluidity.
West Coast container ships waiting to dock fell from 3 to 1, and East Coast backlogs fell from 4 to 2.
West Coast rail intermodal traffic growth accelerated to +16% YoY from +15% the prior week. BNSF was +15% YoY vs +9.7% prior week, UNP was +16% vs +20%.

Rail service metrics were mixed. UNP dwell rose from 19.6 to 19.7 hours, BNSF dwell fell from 23.1 to 22.6 hours. BNSF intermodal velocity was -12% YoY vs -5.6% prior, UNP velocity was -1.9% vs -4.3%.
Ocean container rates China to US West Coast were up about 3% WoW and +203% YoY. The prior week was about $8.25k per FEU (+179% YoY), down about 1% from about $8.34k.
Chassis street dwell was unchanged at 4.0 days for 20ft and 5.9 days for 40/45ft, well below peak congestion.

September lagged data was mixed. San Pedro Bay container dwell rose to about 3.2 days from 3.0 in August, and rail container dwell rose to 7.2 days from 6.8, still far below the 2022 peak of about 16 days.
Big Three West Coast ports inbound loaded containers were +23% YoY in September.
China to US door-to-door shipping averaged 47 days in October, versus 80+ days at peak congestion and 46 in September.
Trucking employment was about 4% below pre-Covid highs in September but showed the first positive YoY growth in 40 months.
LMI transportation capacity contracted faster in September (34.4 vs 40.0) and warehouse capacity fell to 39.3. Warehouse utilization expanded to 64.3 vs 59.6.

GS says if supply chain pressures keep easing, the index could stay more consistently in the '1' territory in 2026. The key question is the effect of tariffs and geopolitical conflicts on freight demand and timing.

sector_views.rationale: Congestion remains muted near pre-Covid fluidity, with tariff and geopolitical effects on freight flows the key uncertainty.
